# Vehicle Inspection FAQ: Process, Reports & Preparation


[Dealer Operations](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/dealer-operations/) |[Product + Tech](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/product-tech/)


3 mins


Oct 14, 2026


A thorough vehicle inspection helps Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), lessors, fleet and rental operators, dealers and remarketing teams understand and document vehicle conditions. Whether managing an off-lease return, evaluating a vehicle for Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) eligibility or preparing inventory for wholesale remarketing, a consistent vehicle inspection process helps support informed decisions.


Below are answers to common questions about the vehicle inspection process.


## What makes a consistent commercial vehicle inspection process valuable?


At its core, a reliable vehicle inspection process combines standardized protocols, documented vehicle condition, images and reporting. Businesses handle off-lease vehicles, CPO inventory, and remarketing operations. A consistent process creates a dependable foundation to manage condition information and support vehicle transitions. Using the same commercial vehicle inspection checklist each time strengthens compliance and transparency.


## Who needs commercial vehicle inspections?


OEMs, captive finance companies, lessors, fleet and rental operators, dealers and remarketing teams use vehicle inspections to understand a vehicle’s condition before it is returned, reviewed for compliance or prepared for sale.


## What types of vehicle inspections are available?


Commercial vehicle inspections can include off-lease condition reviews, compliance reviews, and reporting that helps prepare vehicles for remarketing.


OPENLANE Inspections supports these commercial inspection needs, including:


- **Off-lease and lease-return vehicle inspections** for vehicles approaching lease return or remarketing.
- **CPO compliance reviews** to help OEMs and dealers verify that eligible vehicles meet the inspection and condition requirements of a Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) program.
- **Vehicle remarketing inspections** that document vehicle condition, equipment, damage and images to inform wholesale valuation and resale decisions.


## What is included in a standard off-lease inspection report?


An off-lease vehicle condition report creates a detailed record. It tracks the car’s condition, equipment, and visible damage at the time of inspection. A standard report includes:


- VIN, odometer and equipment listing
- A survey of interior and exterior condition
- Visual inspection for body repairs or repaints, supported by digital paint-depth readings
- Listing and testing of optional equipment or value-affecting add-ons, such as a power roof, roof rack, DVD player or navigation system
- Engine start-up, bringing the engine to operating temperature and engaging the transmission
- Tire measurements and a check for matching brand, size and ratings
- At least 26 high-resolution digital images


## Who is qualified to conduct a commercial vehicle inspection?


Vehicle inspections should be performed by experienced vehicle inspectors who follow a standardized vehicle inspection process and an approved commercial vehicle inspection checklist. OPENLANE Inspections uses experienced inspectors who document conditions consistently with photos, measurements and verified procedures.


## How often should a commercial vehicle inspection be performed?


Inspection frequency depends on the program and purpose. Off-lease inspections typically occur near lease return, while CPO and remarketing inspections occur as vehicles are prepared for certification or resale.


## Why are photos and condition documentation important in a commercial vehicle inspection?


Condition documentation gives commercial sellers and remarketing teams a more consistent view of a vehicle’s current state. High-resolution images, equipment details, tire information and documented interior and exterior observations can help establish a clearer vehicle record for downstream evaluation and sale preparation. This transparency supports arbitration and buyer confidence within the vehicle inspection process.


## How should a vehicle be prepared before an inspection?


Before the scheduled inspection, prepare the vehicle by:


- Removing personal belongings and large objects
- Making both sets of keys available
- Including the owner’s manual
- Removing the cargo cover
- Reinstalling the original tires and/or winter tires, as applicable
- Including charging equipment for applicable vehicles


Taking these steps helps ensure the inspector can document the vehicle and its equipment efficiently.


## How long does a vehicle inspection take?


An OPENLANE vehicle inspection varies based on the type of inspection. Appointments are booked within a two-to-four hour service window.


## What information is needed to schedule a vehicle inspection?


To schedule an inspection, have the last eight digits of the vehicle identification number (VIN) and either the inspection ID or the Lease Account/Reference Number available.
